title: Wonderful Life
year_note: First released in September 1986 on Ugly Man Records, when it reached 72 in the UK. A&M reissued it on 14 August 1987 and it went to 8. It was then the title track of the 1987 album.

notes.made: Colin Vearncombe, a Liverpool art student who called himself Black because he thought nobody would remember his surname, wrote it in 1985. Dave 'Dix' Dickie produced it and played keyboards and programming. Roy Corkill played fretless bass, Jimmy Hughes drums, Martin Green saxophone, and the Sidwell Brothers the brass. It was recorded across three studios: Powerplant in London, Square One in Bury and Pink in Liverpool.
notes.context: By the end of 1985 Vearncombe had been dropped by WEA, been in two car crashes, split from his first wife and was homeless, and he has said the title was sarcastic and most people took it at face value. Ugly Man's single got him signed to A&M, and after 'Sweetest Smile' went top ten the reissue went to 8 in the UK, 2 in France and West Germany and 1 in Austria. Adverts kept it alive for decades, and Katie Melua's 2015 cover fronted a £25 million Premier Inn campaign.

listen_for.note: Vearncombe wrote it in a minor key, which is the joke: a song called 'Wonderful Life' that doesn't sound happy. The Guardian later called his voice a 'slightly frayed baritone'.
Roy Corkill's fretless bass, sliding between notes. It's the same instrument doing the same job as on the 1985 records earlier on this list.
Martin Green's saxophone and the Sidwell Brothers' brass, real players on what started as an indie single.

leads_to.title: Jailhouse Rock
leads_to.why: Vearncombe decided to become a musician after seeing Presley in the 1957 film of the same name, which is a long way from where he ended up.

notes.unverified: The personnel list on Wikipedia comes from the single's liner notes and AllMusic; I couldn't confirm whether the 1987 A&M reissue is the same recording as the 1986 Ugly Man single, so I didn't say either way. The video's 1988 New York Film Festival award isn't named anywhere I could find.

culture.title: Second time lucky
culture.line: The Ugly Man single reached 72 in September 1986. A&M's reissue of 14 August 1987 went to 8 in the UK, 2 in France and West Germany and 1 in Austria.

culture.title: Black and white on Merseyside
culture.line: Gerard de Thame shot the video in Southport and Wallasey, with New Brighton Lighthouse and the Looping Star rollercoaster at Pleasureland. It won an award at the New York Film Festival in 1988.

culture.title: Katie Melua for Premier Inn
culture.line: Katie Melua's 2015 cover soundtracked a £25 million Premier Inn campaign, and Mathilde Santing's 1999 version made the Dutch top 10.
